hamilton.title: The Dutch provinces merge their debts
hamilton.line: The Batavian Republic’s 1798 constitution declared the debts of the old Dutch provinces, mostly Holland’s, national debts of the whole Batavian people.

hamilton.title: Belgium shares the Dutch national debt
hamilton.line: In the new Kingdom of the Netherlands, Belgians shared a large Dutch debt they had not run up, a lasting grievance.

mania.title: US states default after a canal boom
mania.line: US states borrowed for canals and railways, expecting tolls to repay the loans; after the 1837 panic, Indiana, Pennsylvania and others defaulted.

commune.title: Laon’s commune rises against its bishop
commune.line: Laon’s townspeople obtained a commune charter; when their bishop paid the king to revoke it, they rose up and killed him.

commune.title: The Maillotins revolt against a new tax
commune.line: When young Charles VI’s regents imposed a new sales tax, Parisians seized mallets from the city hall and attacked tax collectors.

trusts.title: Athens tries its grain dealers’ cartel
trusts.line: Athens tried grain dealers who colluded to buy cheaply from importers and hoarded grain, one of the earliest recorded antitrust trials.

trusts.title: Emperor Zeno outlaws monopolies
trusts.line: Eastern Roman Emperor Zeno banned monopolies and price-fixing pacts, even those earlier emperors had granted, on pain of confiscation and exile.

modelt.title: Stephenson’s Rocket wins the Rainhill Trials
modelt.line: Stephenson’s Rocket won the Rainhill Trials, and the Liverpool and Manchester steam railway was soon carrying 1,200 passengers a day.

flu.title: The Plague of Athens
flu.line: Thucydides says a plague from Ethiopia, via Egypt, first struck Athens at its port, Piraeus; about a quarter of Athenians died.

flu.title: The Plague of Cyprian
flu.line: A new disease spread from Egypt across the Roman Empire, reaching Rome by 251, where up to 5,000 a day reportedly died.

flu.title: The great smallpox epidemic in Japan
flu.line: Smallpox, reportedly carried from Korea by a fisherman, reached the capital with travelling officials and killed perhaps a third of Japan’s people.

bankrun.title: Runs topple Venice’s biggest banks
bankrun.line: Amid war costs and rumours, depositors rushed Venice’s banks; the Garzoni failed, and three of four main banks collapsed by 1500.

bankrun.title: The Panic of 1907
bankrun.line: Depositors pulled $8 million from New York’s Knickerbocker Trust within three hours; J. P. Morgan rallied bankers to stop the runs.

einstein.title: Leonardo keeps an underwater invention secret
einstein.line: In his notebooks, Leonardo withheld his method of staying underwater “by reason of the evil nature of men,” who might sink ships.

sputnik.title: Rome races to build a navy
sputnik.line: According to Polybius, Rome, a land power outmatched at sea by Carthage, copied a stranded Carthaginian warship and built 120 warships.

saigon.title: Athens’ doomed retreat from Sicily
saigon.line: After failing to take Syracuse, some 40,000 Athenians, allies and camp followers fled overland; nearly all were killed or captured.

saigon.title: Crusaders flee the fall of Acre
saigon.line: Mamluks stormed Acre, the crusader kingdom’s capital; in a chaotic flight to the ships, the rich paid fortunes for passage.

saigon.title: The last Yuan emperor flees Beijing
saigon.line: As Ming armies neared, the last Yuan emperor abandoned Dadu, today’s Beijing, and fled north, ending Mongol rule over China.

netscape.title: France gives photography free to the world
netscape.line: France bought Daguerre’s process and gave it free to the world; by 1853 Americans made an estimated three million daguerreotypes a year.

dotcom.title: England’s patent share boom bursts
dotcom.line: In London’s first stock market boom, investors rushed into firms with new patents such as diving engines; few survived the decade.
